[[File:Decipher.com Hoth Contest 1996.jpg|thumb|Hoth Contest graphic, November 1996.]]
[[Decipher.com]] ran online contests for the [[Star Wars CCG]] from 1996, including daily card-title puzzles, website Easter egg hunts and fan design contests.

== Hoth Contest (1996) ==
The 1996 Hoth Contest posted a daily anagram of a preview card's title.<ref>[http://games.decipher.com/hothcontest/index.html Hoth Contest], Decipher (1996). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19961102055122/http://games.decipher.com/hothcontest/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> A wind sound file played on the contest page.

Recovered daily pages include:

== Easter Egg Hunt (1997) ==
The ''What's New'' area (<code>/new/</code>) ran the Decipher Easter Egg Hunt, with one egg hidden on the website each weekday from 21 to 31 March 1997.<ref>[http://www.decipher.com/new/easteregghunt97/index.html The Decipher Easter Egg Hunt 1997], Decipher (March 1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19970327205157/http://www.decipher.com:80/new/easteregghunt97/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> The Hoth Easter egg hunt closed on 19 December 1997 with two eggs never found.<ref>[http://decipher.com/insidedecipher/archives/1997/hothcontestcloses.html Hoth Easter Egg Contest Closes], Decipher (19 December 1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19990127105320/http://decipher.com/insidedecipher/archives/1997/hothcontestcloses.html Internet Archive]</ref>

== Dagobah Contest (1997) ==
[[File:Decipher.com Dagobah Contest 1997 header.jpg|thumb|The Dagobah Contest, March 1997.]]
The March 1997 Dagobah Contest posted five Shockwave puzzles of preview Dagobah cards.<ref name="dagobah">[http://rothko.decipher.com/new/dagobahcontest/index.html The Dagobah Contest], Decipher (March 1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19970327204942/http://rothko.decipher.com/new/dagobahcontest/index.html Internet Archive]</ref> Each Shockwave movie was a 4-by-6 sliding-tile puzzle. Decipher added one letter a day to each card title.<ref name="p1">[http://rothko.decipher.com/new/dagobahcontest/puzzle1.html Puzzle 1], Decipher (March 1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19970327214142/http://rothko.decipher.com/new/dagobahcontest/puzzle1.html Internet Archive]</ref> Decipher posted the assembled cards for players without Shockwave.<ref name="sol">[http://www.decipher.com/starwars/diversions/theattic/dagobahcontest/solution1b.html The Dagobah Contest], Decipher (17 March 1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19970607212621/http://www.decipher.com:80/starwars/diversions/theattic/dagobahcontest/solution1b.html Internet Archive]</ref> Playable HTML copies of all five sliders are at [https://wiki.swccg.com/preserved/dagobah-contest/ the Dagobah Contest puzzles].

Five first-correct players each won a display box of white-border Premiere packs: Charles Lee, Robert Frost, Matt Hankinson, Jeff McRae and Tim Collins.<ref name="dagobah" /> Five more display boxes went to a random draw from eligible entries. Scott Randel of Riverside, California won the bonus prize, a display box of Dagobah.

== Design a Card (1997) ==
A Design a Card contest for Special Edition closed on 14 April 1997.<ref>[http://www.decipher.com/new/cardcontest/index.html Design a Card Contest!], Decipher (1997). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19981206081227/http://www.decipher.com:80/new/cardcontest/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>

== Endor hidden cards (1999) ==
In 1999 an Endor "hidden cards" contest asked players to name five Endor cards hidden in forest artwork.<ref>[http://www.decipher.com/calendars/product/1999/endor/hiddencards/index.html The DECIPHER Calendar: Spotlight – Hidden Endor cards], Decipher (1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/19990828214243/http://www.decipher.com:80/calendars/product/1999/endor/hiddencards/index.html Internet Archive]</ref>
